claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with hierarchical dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups occur at internal boundaries in the untreated alloy.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries generate local stress concentrations.
The local stress concentrations promote microcracking and catastrophic damage during straining.
The proposed intervention is a post-solidification, low-temperature anneal below the solvus for a controlled time in an inert atmosphere.
The proposed anneal will induce nanoscale precipitates at lamellar colony interfaces.
The proposed anneal can form interfacial precipitates without altering the overall lamellar morphology.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as intermediary sites that facilitate dislocation transmission across internal boundaries.
Facilitated dislocation transmission will reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups will lower local stress concentrations.
Lower local stress concentrations will alleviate microcracking and catastrophic damage.
The nanoscale precipitates will provide precipitation strengthening.
The annealed alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain or slightly increase yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain or slightly increase ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted behavior is scoped to room-temperature tensile loading under ambient conditions.
The predicted behavior applies only when processing preserves the overall lamellar colony architecture.
